title: Oṃ tat sat: the offering of the act

words.role: with sat: the formula tat sat, naming Brahman

words.gram: present participle of √अस्, n. nom. sg.

translation.literal: That, the real: let (this) be an offering to Brahman.
translation.readable: Tat sat — may this be offered to Brahman.

units.pause_note: M writes तत्सत् ब्रह्मार्पणमस्तु with a pause after तत्सत् (the formula is said as two phrases), so the t stays unvoiced before b; joined without a pause it would be तत्सद्ब्रह्मार्पणमस्तु.

meaning: The closing words of the samarpaṇa in the Mylapore prayoga: after kāyena vācā offers everything done to Nārāyaṇa, tat sat names the absolute, and the act is declared an offering to Brahman. Om tat sat as a designation of Brahman is the formula discussed in the Bhagavad Gītā (17.23); the witness itself names no source for this line.
in_the_rite: Step samarpana, after kāyena vācā (M only; S ends with kāyena vācā).
